reason: Gravity should help dense metal separate from the molten silicate.

effect: The metal now forms droplets within the silicate melt, ready for separation.
reaction: The intermediate makes the physical process clearer.
reason: Gravity should pull the dense metal droplets downward through the melt.

reason: The next ingredient for completing the interior is not clear, so I’ll check the sinking metal’s available partners.

reaction: The connection between convection and heat loss is clear.
reason: Radiation escaping into space should cool the surface melt and help form crust.

effect: Radiative cooling formed crystals in a surface layer above the hot, moving rock.
reaction: The thin solid layer makes the beginning of crust formation clear.
reason: The next step toward floating crustal rafts is not certain, so I’ll check what the crystals can combine with.

choice.inspect: Crystals in a cooling surface layer

expectation: The inspection should reveal how the crystals develop into crustal rafts.

effect: Inspecting the crystals automatically combined them with surface melt, forming fragile crustal rafts and completing the chapter.
reaction: The temporary, uneven nature of the first crust was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating metal droplets under gravity and completing the core made differentiation understandable as a process within the same planet.

leastWorthwhile.text: The unsuccessful attempt to apply gravity directly to the magma ocean was a small detour, although the feedback identified useful partners.

surprise.text: The first crust formed as fragile, temporary rafts rather than a permanent continuous surface.

arbitrary.text: Combining the sinking metal back with the magma ocean was not obvious beforehand, though the result explained it as differentiation within the same planet.

continue.text: Yes. The physical explanations made the construction satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the early surface develops.
